description: TaskService.get_page slices `self._tasks[start:end - 1]` instead of `self._tasks[start:end]`, an off-by-one that silently drops the last task on every page returned to callers.

TaskDB.find_by_owner builds a SQL query with `"SELECT * FROM tasks WHERE owner = '%s'" % owner`, directly interpolating unsanitized user-supplied `owner` input into the query string instead of using a parameterized query, which is a classic SQL injection vector.

The module-level `_job_status` dict is read and read-modify-written by `start_job` and `finish_job`, both explicitly documented as called concurrently from multiple worker threads/tasks, with no lock guarding the shared dict, so concurrent updates for different jobs can interleave and corrupt job status.

find_first_match opens `path` with `open(path, "r")` (no `with` block) and, when `keyword` matches, `return line.strip()` fires before the `f.close()` on the line after the loop, so the file handle leaks on the (common) early-return path.

send_reminder uses a bare `except: pass` around the transport.send call, silently swallowing every possible error (network failure, bad address, misconfigured transport) with no logging, so failed reminders vanish without a trace.

build_vip_report does `if task.owner in vip_owners` inside a loop over `tasks`, where `vip_owners` is a plain list, giving O(len(tasks) * len(vip_owners)) time; converting vip_owners to a set once up front would make it O(len(tasks)).

make_filename_slug hand-rolls a character-by-character slugify loop that duplicates app.utils.text_utils.slugify (the canonical helper already in this repo) instead of calling it, letting the two implementations silently drift out of sync.
